en: She passed the exam last year.
tamil: அவ போன வருஷம் தேர்வுல பாஸ் ஆனா.
explain: Use past simple with 'last year'. Do not say 'she has passed last year'.

en: He is senior to me.
explain: Senior, junior and superior take 'to', not 'than'. Do not say 'senior than me'.

en: I am fed up with this traffic.
tamil: இந்த டிராபிக்கால நான் ரொம்ப சலிச்சுப் போயிட்டேன்.
explain: The phrase is 'fed up with' something. Do not say 'fed up of'.

en: She is interested in music.
explain: Use 'interested in'. Do not say 'interested on' or 'interested about'.

en: I am waiting for the bus.
context: Replying to a call from the bus stop.
explain: 'Wait' needs 'for' before the thing you wait for. Do not leave out 'for'.

en: Could you lend me a pen?
tamil: உங்க பேனாவை எனக்கு கொஞ்சம் கடன் கொடுக்கறீங்களா?
context: Asking someone for a small favour.
explain: The giver 'lends' and you 'borrow'. Do not say 'borrow me a pen'.

en: I enjoyed the movie very much.
context: Talking about a film you saw.
explain: 'Enjoy' needs an object. Say 'enjoyed the movie' or 'enjoyed it', not just 'enjoyed'.

en: My phone is not working properly.
context: Telling someone about a faulty phone.
explain: Use 'is not working' or 'does not work'. 'Working' here means functioning.

en: How was your weekend trip?
tamil: உன் வார இறுதி டிரிப் எப்படி இருந்துச்சு?
explain: Use past 'was' for a finished weekend. Do not say 'how is your weekend?'.

en: I want to learn English.
explain: 'Want' is followed by 'to' plus a verb. Do not say 'I want learn' or 'I want that I learn'.

en: He is a very honest person.
explain: Use 'a' before a singular noun. Honest starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an' only for the word itself.

en: I have two brothers and a sister.
tamil: எனக்கு ரெண்டு அண்ணன் தம்பிங்களும் ஒரு தங்கச்சியும் இருக்காங்க.
explain: Use plural nouns after numbers (two brothers). Use 'a' with one sister.

en: Please reply to my message.
explain: The verb 'reply' needs 'to'. Do not say 'reply my message'.

en: We reached the hotel at night.
explain: 'Reach' does not need 'to'. Do not say 'reached to the hotel'.

en: She entered the room quietly.
explain: 'Enter' does not need 'into'. Say 'entered the room'.

en: He is much taller than me.
explain: Do not say 'more taller'. Add -er to short adjectives and use 'much' for emphasis.

en: I will do it myself.
context: Offering to handle a task alone.
explain: Use 'myself' to stress you do it alone. Do not say 'by myself only'.

en: Did you finish your homework?
explain: Use 'did' plus the base verb. Do not say 'did you finished'.

en: I have a headache, so I am going home early.
tamil: எனக்கு தலைவலி, அதனால சீக்கிரம் வீட்டுக்கு போறேன்.
context: Telling your manager you are leaving.
explain: Say 'I have a headache'. Do not say 'I am having headache'. Use 'a' before headache.

en: I am not going to the party tomorrow.
explain: Use 'going to' for plans. Add 'not' after 'am'. Do not say 'I am not go'.
